headlines.full_text: Children killed while they slept as Russian missile kills 19 in block of flats Five children are among the victims of a strike that destroyed 30 flats in northern Ukraine as families slept. A Russian missile has killed 19 people including five children in an apartment block in northern Ukraine, destroying 30 flats as families slept. Three of the children were one-year-olds in the attack on Pryluky, east of Kyiv, early on Wednesday, and one of the boys died with his mother and grandmother, officials said. Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky said it was one of Russia's "most vile strikes", and suggested the Russian military had carried it out as a "birthday gift" to Vladimir Putin, who turned 74 on Wednesday. Moscow made no mention of the attack on Pryluky but said its "massive strike" had targeted military industries in Kyiv and elsewhere. Across the country, the death toll on Wednesday climbed to 25, as Russian strikes claimed two lives in the capital, two in Kremenchuk, and two more in Oleksandriya. More than 430 apartments and private homes were damaged and dozens of people were injured in the attack on the central city of Kremenchuk, the regional leader said. Rescue teams in Pryluky spent hours searching for victims in the rubble of a five-storey block of flats. Late in the afternoon rescuers said the body of a fifth child had been found at the scene. More than 50 residents were wounded in the attack that also damaged other residential buildings as well as a youth centre. headlines.full_text:
Ex-Google boss warns Ukraine over Russia’s ‘Starlink rival’ The Rassvet satellite network could give Moscow immense advantages in the Ukraine conflict, Eric Schmidt has said
Read Full Article at RT.com Russia’s emerging Rassvet satellite network – often described as a“Starlink rival”– could provide Moscow’s military with sustainable communications and data to attack any target in Ukraine at will, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt has warned. Speaking to The Economist last week, Schmidt noted that while Ukraine was initially seen as the main innovator in the conflict, Russia had largely closed that gap while pressing its advantage with far greater resources. Schmidt noted that one of these domains is Russia’s Rassvet satellite project, which he suggested was about a year from maturity.“Once that network is in place, it is more or less unblockable,”he warned, adding that this could let Russian forces“hunt anywhere”inside Ukraine. The ex-Google CEO also weighed in on the idea of granting Ukraine access to Starlink over Russia, which could allow Kiev to rely on Elon Musk’s satellites to target oil refineries and civilian infrastructure, calling it“really a political decision.” “It’s really a government decision. And the US government needs to grapple with this question,”he said. Developed by private Russian aerospace firm Bureau 1440, part of the IKS Holding conglomerate, Rassvet debuted in 2023 with the launch of three experimental satellites. The network is designed to offer speeds of up to 1Gbps with latency below 70 milliseconds and to operate at an orbit of around 800 km – higher than that of Starlink to balance the number of satellites against an increased coverage area. headlines.title: NATO nation decries drone strikes on merchant vessels off its coast
headlines.full_text:
NATO nation decries drone strikes on merchant vessels off its coast Two merchant vessels have been hit by unknown drones within Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone in the Black Sea
Read Full Article at RT.com Two commercial vessels were hit by unidentified drones on Tuesday off the Bulgarian coast in the Black Sea, Prime Minister Rumen Radev has confirmed. The attack marks the first time when merchant vessels were attacked within the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of a NATO member in the waterway. Such zones have a unique legal status and are adjacent to a country’s territorial waters, with the area being neither fully under its sovereignty or categorized as international open waters. “This is an unacceptable attack in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone. It is a blatant violation of international law and maritime law,”Radev said while speaking after an emergency government meeting to assess the incident. The vessels, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan and the Palau-flagged Able, were hit overnight around 80 miles (128 kilometers) off Bulgaria’s coast by unknown sea and aerial drones, according to the PM, who did not immediately assign the blame to any party. The Alfa Watan, which was sailing to Romania from Egypt, sustained critical damage, sinking shortly after the attack with the status of its crew not immediately known, according to Radev. The second vessel, which sailed from Romania to Türkiye, caught fire, and its crew of 18 was rescued by a Bulgarian ferry. Two of the sailors suffered severe injuries and were flown to a hospital in the port city of Varna, Radev noted. “As a state responsible within our exclusive economic zone for the health and lives of anyone navigating in this are
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article attributes the drone strikes to unknown actors, framing them as a violation without specifying responsibility.

headlines.raw_title: Ukraine’s losses from port downtime exceed five billion dollars
headlines.title: Ukraine’s losses from port downtime exceed five billion dollars
headlines.full_text: Ukraine’s losses from port downtime exceed five billion dollars The Odessa port shutdown has been ongoing since July 22 MOSCOW, October 8. /TASS/. Ukraine has lost more than five billion dollars in foreign exchange revenue due to downtime at the Odessa ports, according to TASS calculations. Commercial merchant ships continue to avoid the ports of Odessa, Chernomorsk, and Yuzhny. Only vessels affiliated with the Ukrainian armed forces are calling at those ports. Consequently, maritime trade is being routed through Danube ports - that is, Izmail in Ukraine and Constanta in Romania - which together can potentially handle no more than one-third of the exports that previously passed through the ports of Odessa. As a result, Ukraine exported only 44% of its planned agricultural exports in September. Exports of metallurgical products ceased completely by the end of September. These two commodities together accounted for about 65% of Ukraine’s total exports and about $26 billion in foreign exchange earnings per year. The Odessa port shutdown has been ongoing since July 22.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It presents factual economic data on port shutdown losses without emotive language.

headlines.title: Three DPR residents killed, eight wounded in Ukrainian attacks since start of day
headlines.full_text: Three DPR residents killed, eight wounded in Ukrainian attacks since start of day The attacks damaged three residential buildings, three infrastructure facilities, trucks and passenger cars DONETSK, October 7. /TASS/. Ukrainian forces have killed three civilians and wounded eight others in attacks on the Donetsk People’s Republic (DPR) since the start of the day, the Office for Documenting Ukraine’s War Crimes under the regional administration said. "The total number of casualties is 11: three people were killed and eight wounded," the office said on its Telegram channel. Two people were killed in the village of Spartak on the outskirts of Donetsk. Another person was killed in Gorlovka, where five residents were also wounded. Three people were injured in a Ukrainian attack on the Donetsk-Avdeyevka highway. The attacks damaged three residential buildings, three infrastructure facilities, trucks and passenger cars.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article presents factual casualty figures from a Russian source without emotive language or bias.

headlines.raw_title: EU, NATO to squeeze Kiev regime for everything it has — Russian delegation head
headlines.title: EU, NATO to squeeze Kiev regime for everything it has — Russian delegation head
headlines.full_text: EU, NATO to squeeze Kiev regime for everything it has — Russian delegation head Head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna negotiations on military security and arms control Yulia Zhdanova emphasized that the West primarily "needs experience in high-intensity combat" VIENNA, October 7. /TASS/. EU and NATO countries will use Kiev to serve their own interests to the very end, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna negotiations on military security and arms control Yulia Zhdanova said. "It has long been clear that EU and NATO countries will squeeze the Kiev regime for everything it has to serve their own interests," the diplomat said at the OSCE Forum for Security Co-operation in Vienna. Zhdanova said the West primarily "needs experience in high-intensity combat." She pointed to NATO’s large-scale Avenger Triad 26 exercises, now underway with about 4,000 troops on the eastern flank. The Russian diplomat said the exercises are aimed at improving coordination among allied forces. They will link drones, radars and other weapons systems "into a single network," using information obtained from the Ukrainian military.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The Russian delegation frames EU/NATO as exploiting Ukraine for their own interests, portraying them as corrupt actors.

headlines.raw_title: West should not be surprised by fuel price hikes over Ukraine actions — Russian envoy
headlines.title: West should not be surprised by fuel price hikes over Ukraine actions — Russian envoy
headlines.full_text: West should not be surprised by fuel price hikes over Ukraine actions — Russian envoy Yulia Zhdanova said Kiev has stepped up efforts to block Russian shipping in the Black and Azov Seas at the urging of its Western handlers VIENNA, October 7. /TASS/. Western countries should not be surprised if fuel prices rise after Kiev carries out its plans to block Russian shipping in the Black and Azov Seas, Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna negotiations on military security and arms control, said. Zhdanova said Kiev has stepped up efforts to block Russian shipping in the Black and Azov Seas at the urging of its Western handlers. These measures include attacks on port infrastructure. She added these actions were aimed at disrupting Russian hydrocarbon export logistics and the transportation of civilian cargo. "Do not be surprised later if these actions result in higher fuel prices not only on international markets but also in your countries," the envoy told her colleagues at a meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Co-operation in Vienna.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The envoy attributes fuel price hikes to Ukraine’s actions, scapegoating them for a systemic problem.

headlines.title: Kherson Region children's ombudsman calls UAV blow on car with father of 13 kids terror
headlines.full_text: Kherson Region children's ombudsman calls UAV blow on car with father of 13 kids terror Irina Kravchenko said that there can be no justification for such actions GENICHESK, October 7. /TASS/. The attack of a Ukrainian drone on a car in the Kherson Region, which killed the father of 13 children Alexander Kolotun and his 15-year-old daughter, is a monstrous crime and terror of the Kiev regime, children's ombudsman of the region Irina Kravchenko told TASS. "The Kiev regime has again committed a monstrous act of crime against civilians. This is not an accident or a mistake - it is a deliberate, purposeful policy of terror against one's own people, against families, and against children. The Kiev regime has been killing civilians for years, destroying homes, schools and hospitals, depriving children of their childhood and future. There are lives, destinies and irreparable grief behind every such attack," she said. Kravchenko said that there can be no justification for such actions. "Sooner or later everyone involved in these crimes will answer for what they have done," she added. Earlier, Governor Vladimir Saldo said that Alexander and his daughter were killed 120 km from the contact line near the village of Rykovo. In June, Russian President Vladimir Putin personally presented Alexander's wife Tatyana with the Order of the Mother Heroine. She is currently expecting her fourteenth child. The family is known in the Kherson Region thanks to a small bakery they opened, which supplied bread to residents of the surrounding villages.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article blames the Kiev regime for a drone attack, portraying it as deliberate terror.

headlines.title: West furthers military-industrial interests with OSCE Russia disinformation campaign
headlines.full_text: West furthers military-industrial interests with OSCE Russia disinformation campaign "Even here, within the framework of the OSCE's military-political direction, we have already had the opportunity to see that the Western participating states are not interested in a fact-based professional dialogue," Yulia Zhdanova said VIENNA, October 7. /TASS/. Western member states of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) are fanning a disinformation campaign against Russia used by their governments to promote solutions in the interests of national military industry circles and the militarization of Europe, head of the Russian delegation at the Vienna talks on military security and arms control Yulia Zhdanova said. "Even here, within the framework of the OSCE's military-political direction, we have already had the opportunity to see that the Western participating states are not interested in a fact-based professional dialogue, their goal is to inflate disinformation campaigns that are subsequently used by their governments to push convenient solutions in the interests of the national military-industrial circles and the militarization of the continent," she told a meeting of the OSCE Forum on Security Cooperation. Her speech was made available to TASS.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It accuses Western states of using disinformation to serve military-industrial interests.

headlines.title: Ukrainian drone attack kills father of 13 children, 15-year-old daughter in Kherson Region
headlines.full_text: Ukrainian drone attack kills father of 13 children, 15-year-old daughter in Kherson Region "This morning a Ukrainian drone attacked a passenger car near Rykovo of the Genichesk district," Vladimir Saldo said GENICHESK, October 7. /TASS/. A father of 13 children, along with his 15-year-old daughter were killed on Wednesday after a Ukrainian drone flew into their car in the Kherson Region, Governor Vladimir Saldo said. "This morning a Ukrainian drone attacked a passenger car near Rykovo of the Genichesk district. The car was completely destroyed. Alexander Kolotun and his 15-year-old daughter Anna were killed. Alexander and his wife Tatyana raised 13 children. Tatyana is currently expecting her fourteenth child," he wrote on Max messenger. Saldo said that the tragedy occurred 120 km from the line of contact. The governor recalled that in June, Russian President Vladimir Putin personally presented Tatyana with the Order of the Mother Heroine. "The Kolotun family is well known in the Kherson Region: they opened a small bakery and supplied bread to the residents of the surrounding villages. This is a heinous war crime, a crime against humanity itself. My deepest condolences to Tatyana, the children, and all the relatives and friends of the victims. We will provide all necessary assistance to the family," he added.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece highlights a large family’s loss to evoke sympathy and portray the attack as a heinous war crime.

headlines.raw_title: Russian delegation warns confrontation with West could enter most severe phase
headlines.title: Russian delegation warns confrontation with West could enter most severe phase
headlines.full_text: Russian delegation warns confrontation with West could enter most severe phase According to Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna talks on military security and arms control, Western politicians continue to intensify their military rhetoric VIENNA, October 7. /TASS/. The West’s drive to escalate tensions over Ukraine further increases the risk that its confrontation with Russia could enter its most severe phase, Yulia Zhdanova, head of the Russian delegation to the Vienna talks on military security and arms control, said. According to the diplomat, Western politicians continue to intensify their military rhetoric. She noted that, alongside plans to provide further support to Ukraine and deploy NATO troops there, "Europe is openly discussing preparations for military operations outside the Ukrainian context," as well as increased pressure on Russia. Zhdanova said the EU and NATO’s unwillingness "to pursue genuine diplomacy based on reality and consideration of the interests of all parties" is prompting them "to inflame the situation and raise the stakes." "But the more reckless their course and the more openly they declare the goal of inflicting a ‘strategic defeat’ on their adversary, the greater the risk that the confrontation will enter its most severe phase," the diplomat told a meeting of the OSCE Forum for Security Cooperation. The text of her remarks was obtained by TASS.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article frames Western politicians as escalating tensions and threatening Russia, attributing blame to a specific group.

headlines.full_text: Ukraine Launches One of Its Largest Aerial Attacks of the War, Killing at Least 6 People in Russia Russia’s Ministry of Defense said that it had destroyed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight. headlines.full_text: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies, union says Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September. An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union. Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford rent increases. The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital. "We regret to announce that Maricarmen passed away today," the Madrid Tenants' Union said in a statement, adding her situation marked "a turning point in the history of this country". Union spokesperson Alicia del Río said: "Speculation costs lives, and today rentierism has finished killing our colleague Maricarmen" but "her memory lives on with us". A cause of death was not announced. Abascal's death was received in Puerta del Sol with a big collective gasp, then followed by a minute of silence. It is in this square in the centre of Madrid where thousands have been camping since Abascal's eviction last month to demand more affordable housing. On Wednesday, it became the place to pay tribute to her. People lit dozens of candles around the square in a small improvised vigil that glowed with a warm light on a dry and warm autumn night. headlines.full_text: What is pneumonic plague and how does it spread? The death of a worker from a Russian lab that researches plague has prompted questions about the disease. The World Health Organization has asked Russia for more information on the death of a worker at a Siberian plague research laboratory. It is still not clear exactly what led to the worker falling ill, but media reports have led to a flurry of speculation. Russian officials are still investigating the cause of the death, but they say those who came into contact with the researcher all tested negative for pneumonic plague. So what is pneumonic plague, and how dangerous is it? Pneumonic plague is a really serious lung infection, often described as the most virulent form of plague. There are two other types of plague: bubonic, which affects the lymph nodes; and septicaemic, which affects the blood. Pneumonic plague can occur after an initial infection of one of these other types. Symptoms include shortness of breath, chest pain, and often coughing up blood. It's regarded as being more serious but less common than bubonic plague. The global number of infections of all three types of plague varies each year, but it is probably somewhere between 1,000 to 3,000 cases. Most of these are bubonic plague, and many of them occur in central Africa, but cases also develop in other places, including Russia, India, China, and the United States. Prof Piero Olliaro is Professor of Poverty-Related Infectious Diseases at the University of Oxford. He said: "Plague itself has not disappeared: the bacterium that causes it,Yersinia pestis, persists in animal reservoirs across many parts of the world.

TEHRAN — Washington has a familiar habit: when diplomacy becomes inconvenient, it begins speaking the language of threat. Repeated often enough, that language can transform a political dispute into an emergency that supposedly demands military action. Iraq should have taught the United States how dangerous that habit can be. In 2003, Washington and its allies built the case for invading Iraq around claims that Saddam Hussein possessed weapons of mass destruction. Those warnings were presented with confidence, the threat was described as urgent, and war was framed as necessary. The weapons were never found. The consequences, however, were real. Iraq was destabilized, violence spread and the region was left dealing with the aftermath of a war sold to the public on claims that proved disastrously unreliable. That history matters as Washington and its allies intensify their rhetoric about Iran. Iran is not Iraq, and the two cases should not be treated as identical. Iran has its own political system, strategic capabilities and regional relationships. Its nuclear program was subject to the most intensive inspections before the joint U.S.-Israel attack on Iran that first began in June 2025. Yemen’s rebel Ansar Allah movement - the Houthis - launched ballistic missile strikes on Arab coalition positions south of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree stated. "Over the past 24 hours, our armed forces (the Houthis — TASS) have fired 11 ballistic missiles at 11 concentrations of Saudi forces in areas south of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Al-Suqia, Ras al-Arah and Al-Mudaraba," Saree said in a statement published on his Telegram channel. He also stated that the attacks killed or wounded dozens of people, including commanders, and destroyed numerous pieces of military equipment. He added that another ballistic missile had struck the position of the 13th Al-Amaliqa Brigade, killing or wounding more than 30 enemy fighters. Meanwhile, Arab coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said a ballistic missile launcher used in the recent attack on Riyadh had been destroyed in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa. headlines.full_text: Three killed in attacks on two Saudi airports A Sudanese national was killed in the strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while eight others were injured, including five Saudis, two Egyptians and one Pakistani DOHA, October 7. /TASS/. Three people were killed and 36 others sustained injuries of varying severity in two attacks on international airports in Saudi Arabia, the kingdom’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said. According to the authority, the attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport occurred on October 6 and 7. "Two women, nationals of Morocco and Algeria, were killed in the attack on Abha International Airport, while 28 people were injured," the authority said in a statement. The injured included Saudi nationals and citizens of Bangladesh and the Philippines. A Sudanese national was killed in the strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, while eight others were injured, including five Saudis, two Egyptians and one Pakistani. Their conditions range from minor to critical, and all were taken to hospitals for treatment. The facilities also sustained material damage. Relevant agencies are assessing the consequences of the attacks and taking the necessary measures to ensure the safety of passengers and civil aviation.

Canada says it will indefinitely suspend plans to expand its medically assisted dying law to people whose sole condition is mental illness, citing a lack of consensus on who would be eligible. It comes after a parliamentary panel earlier this year recommended that medically assisted dying - known as Maid in Canada - should not be expanded. On Wednesday, Canada's justice minister, Sean Fraser, said that "while there is not a perfect consensus on this issue, we believe this is the correct approach at this particular time". Supporters of extending the programme to those with mental illness alone argue that not doing so violates their constitutional rights and access to medical care. A federal case remains before the courts challenging the government's earlier decision to delay access to Maid for people with mental illness. Fraser acknowledged this is an issue that the Supreme Court could weigh on in the future. Wednesday's announcement means that Canadians with mental illness as their sole condition will not be able to access assisted dying by March 2027 as previously planned. The government will instead introduce a new law in the coming weeks that suspends that expansion indefinitely, Fraser said. After takeoff, the aircraft climbed to around 10,000 feet before the crew received a tyre-pressure indication and decided to dump fuel before returning to Munich. US mortgage rates have climbed to their highest level in nearly three years, making it more expensive for Americans to buy homes. The average rate on the most common 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA). headlines.full_text: Chemistry Nobel awarded for solving mystery of life's asymmetry The prize was given to the French and Japanese scientists for solving the mystery of life's asymmetry. The Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French scientist Henri B. Kagan and Japan's Kenso Soai for providing a solution to the chemical mystery of life's asymmetry. The researchers discovered how nature exclusively makes the correct version of a molecule - rather than its mirror image. For example, amino acid molecules, the building blocks of proteins, exist as two forms that are each other's mirror image. But living organisms on Earth only function with one of those forms. The Nobel laureates answered the question: why does life favour just one of these mirror image molecules over the other. In organic chemistry, this property is known as "chirality", so chiral molecules have both right and left-handed forms. You can think of them as looking like our hands - not identical, but each a mirror image of the other. And while nature almost exclusively produces the version it requires to function, chemical reactions in a lab usually create a 50-50 mix of both left- and right-handed molecules. "Up to 100 troops will be deployed to the border," he said in an interview with national radio LRT. According to the defense minister, the army will be stationed at the border for the next few weeks. The Defense Ministry’s decision came in response to a request from Interior Minister Martynas Katelynas to strengthen security along the border with the Kaliningrad Region. In his appeal to the defense minister, Katelynas said he had been forced to seek assistance in view of the overall security situation in the region. The interior minister called the deployment of troops to the border a preventive measure.

headlines.full_text: Trump Says US and Canada Have Reached Last-Minute Deal to Delay 50% US Tariffs on Canadian Imports The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies. Washington:President Donald Trump said Tuesday he was delaying 50% U.S. tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal hours before the sanctions were to go into effect. The announcement, which Trump made on his social media platform, buys time for more negotiations and avoids, for now, another strain in already tense relations between the historic allies. “I have paused the 50% Tariffs against Canada, that were scheduled to kick in tomorrow morning for three days, based on the fact that Canada and the U.S.A., subject to the finalisation of documents, have a DEAL!” Trump posted on Truth Social less than two hours before the 12:01 a.m. Wednesday deadline. If they had gone into effect as scheduled at 12:01 a.m. Wednesday, Trump’s import taxes would have hit Canadian products ranging from hockey sticks to tongue depressors. But the political impact would likely have been bigger than the economic one. Canada had threatened to retaliate against any new tariffs with levies of its own, aggravating a trade fight between countries that sold each other $880 billion worth of goods and services last year. Canadian officials did not immediately respond to requests for comment Tuesday night. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Trump had spoken twice by phone in the past two days about the ongoing negotiations, including a call Tuesday afternoon, Carney’s office said, underscoring the last-minute push for a deal. headlines.full_text: 'Substantial Progress Made': Canadian PM Carney as American Tariffs Postponed for 3 Days Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home. Ottawa:With Ottawa and Washington continually engaged in discussions over the 50 per cent tariff on a select range of Canadian goods, Prime Minister Mark Carney said that the implementation of the tariffs has been postponed until August 21. Sharing the remarks in a letter posted on X, Prime Minister Carney reassured that while rigorous engagements remain in place with Washington, Canada remains focused on building a stronger, more independent, and more competitive economy at home. "Over the last number of weeks, Canada has engaged in intensive discussions with the United States to address outstanding trade issues and deliver greater certainty and real benefits for Canadian businesses, workers, farmers and families," he said. The Canadian Prime Minister observed that while significant headway has been made, key work remains to be done. Substantial progress has been made, although there is important work still to be done. As this work is ongoing, the United States has agreed to postpone the implementation of its 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods under Section 338 of the U.S. Tariff Act of 1930 until the end of day, August 21," he said. The announcement comes in the nick of time as the Trump administration's latest round of tariffs was originally scheduled to take effect at 12:01 a.m. Eastern Time on Wednesday. According to Canadian public broadcaster CBC, the levies would have applied to hundreds of products worth more than USD 28 billion, from plywood and cement to wine
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece reports Canada’s tariff postponement factually, with no emotive or biased language.

headlines.full_text: Pakistan's Supreme Court Orders Former PM Imran Khan to Be Moved to Hospital from Jail Amid Health Concerns The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered former Prime Minister Imran Khan to be moved to a hospital from jail due to health concerns. He has been imprisoned since August 2023 and faces multiple cases following his ousting in 2022. Islamabad:The Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered on Tuesday that former Prime Minister Imran Khan ​be moved to a hospital from jail, his Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party ‌said, meeting a longstanding demand of his party and family, who had raised concerns about his health. Cricketer-turned-politician Khan, 73, has been in jail since August ​2023, convicted in a string of cases that he ​says were politically driven following his ouster in 2022. A three-member Supreme Court bench, headed by Justice Shahid Wahid and comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, issued the ruling on Imran's petition for his hospitalisation. His sons ⁠repeatedly expressed concern regarding his deteriorating health last year, with his ​lawyers saying he had lost significant vision in his right eye ​while in prison. "It's a very welcome order, and we wish it had happened sooner so his eye and general health would not have deteriorated this much," ​PTI spokesperson Zulfikar Bukhari said. "He should remain in hospital until all ​doctors are satisfied," he said. The court has directed Khan be moved to Shifa ‌International ⁠Hospital within 48 hours and remain there until September 16, Khan's spokesperson Naeem Haider Panjutha said on X. Since he lost power in a no-confidence vote, Khan has faced multiple cases, including over state ​gifts and an ​unlawful marriage. The review, which examined voting records, public statements and campaign material, found candidates in 41 of the 62 competitive congressional races attempting to create some distance from Trump. Most of the candidates have not rejected Trump's broader political agenda or openly challenged his leadership of the Republican Party. Instead, they have chosen to diverge from him on individual issues, apparently seeking to appeal to independent voters while avoiding a direct confrontation with the president. Policy disagreements emerged as the most common form of separation, with such differences appearing in 23 of the 62 competitive races reviewed byReuters. The Iran conflict was at the centre of disagreements in 12 contests. headlines.full_text: US midterms: These 5 House races could determine control of Congress in 2026 With Democrats needing only four net gains for a House majority, even a small number of these closely fought races could have an outsized impact With Democrats needing only four net gains for a House majority, even a small number of these closely fought races could have an outsized impact The fight for control of the US House of Representatives could come down to a small group of highly competitive districts in the November 3 midterm elections. Republicanscurrently hold a narrow 219-214 majority(two seats are vacant), meaning Democrats need a net gain of just four seats to take control of the chamber. That makes closely divided districts particularly important. WhileDemocrats are targeting dozens of Republican-held seats, Republicans are also trying to protect vulnerable incumbents and defend districts that have become more competitive after redistricting. Five races in Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine illustrate how narrow the path to a House majority could be. Democratic Representative Vicente Gonzalez is seeking another term against Republican Eric Flores in Texas’ 34th Congressional District. The race has become more competitive after Texas redrew the district during the mid-decade redistricting process. Under the new boundaries, the district became significantly more favourable to Republicans, with Donald Trump estimated to have carried it by about 10 points in 2024.
